title: Namespace, Secret, restart
prompt: Fill in the blanks to create the `notes` namespace and make it your default, store the database password in a Secret, decode it to prove it's only base64, and restart notes-api so it picks up changed environment variables.
hints: The kind of object you're creating first is also the name of the `set-context` flag.
The Secret type for arbitrary key-value pairs is the opposite of "specific".
`base64` decodes with a short flag; `kubectl rollout` has a subcommand that replaces Pods without changing the template by hand.
explanation:
```bash
kubectl create namespace notes
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=notes
kubectl create secret generic notes-db --from-literal=POSTGRES_PASSWORD=dev-only-change-me
kubectl get secret notes-db -o jsonpath='{.data.POSTGRES_PASSWORD}' | base64 -d
kubectl rollout restart deployment/notes-api
```
`generic` is the Secret type for arbitrary keys (others include `tls` and `docker-registry`). The decode step shows why Secret manifests must never be committed. `rollout restart` replaces Pods gradually, and the new ones read the current ConfigMap and Secret values at start.
